project_type: Full-stack web application (MERN) — portfolio / skills-demonstration project

production_status.note: Intended for adoption by a Nigerian diaspora community active on Twitter/X. Never pitched; the community entered a leadership dispute and the owner repositioned the work as a portfolio project. No adoption, volume, revenue, reliability or business-impact metric exists or may be claimed.

project_description: A community-management platform for a diaspora community organisation: member register with four-tier role-based access control, six-path authentication with device-based step-up verification, an online election system with multiple concurrent polls and verified voters, Twitter Spaces and physical event scheduling, sub-groups, and dual payment-provider integration (Stripe + GoCardless). Built solo, containerised, and deployed publicly.

authorship.author: Akintola Abraham <abramseyakid@gmail.com>
authorship.qualification: Solo project — no code review, no PR workflow, no team process.

architecture.pattern: Monolith — single Node process serves the REST API and the Vite-built SPA from one origin
architecture.frontend_pattern: Per-domain triad: <domain>Service.js (axios) + <domain>Slice.js (createAsyncThunk) + <domain>FilterSlice.js (client-side search), composed in a 16-reducer Redux store
architecture.auth_mechanism: JWT in HTTP-only, secure, sameSite:none cookie; 1-day cookie expiry, 7-day JWT expiry
architecture.spa_serving: Custom fallback middleware distinguishes asset extensions from client routes and returns dist/index.html with anti-cache headers
architecture.webhook_handling: POST /api/payment/webhook registered with express.raw() before the global express.json() so Stripe signature verification sees unparsed bytes

workflows: Login from unknown user-agent → encrypted 6-digit code emailed, 60-minute expiry → /sendLoginCode → /loginWithCode → session issued
Profile-completeness gate blocks all dashboard routes until UK address fields are filled

Election lifecycle: create election → create polls (inherit election window) → add candidates (exclusive across sibling polls) → admin verifies voters → members vote while now <= endDateTime, may change vote → counts concealed from role 'user' until poll closes

Payment: create Checkout Session (payment or subscription + trial) → Stripe-hosted checkout → redirect to /paymentsuccess/success/{SESSION_ID} → client saves details with server-resolved product name; webhook independently fulfils checkout.session.completed and computes trial + 1-year expiry
Spaces / Events / Groups: author-only CRUD with unique url, slug, and append-only edit audit trail

my_contributions.detail: 8 Mongoose schemas with validation, unique constraints, soft-delete flags and createdBy/updatedBy[] audit trails
1,409-line auth controller implementing six sign-in paths plus device-fingerprint step-up verification
Four-tier RBAC enforced server-side on every mutating route and mirrored in client route/component guards
7 routers, 59 route handlers plus a raw-body webhook endpoint
Cross-poll candidate exclusivity, vote transfer with count reconciliation, verified-voter gating, concealed live results, VersionError retry
Stripe + GoCardless integration behind one Payment model, webhook-driven fulfilment, server-side product resolution
Handlebars-templated transactional email with two provider implementations; migrated Gmail OAuth2 → Brevo without changing call sites
79 React source files, ~10,650 LOC — routing, protected routes, profile gate, search, pagination, modals, toasts, dashboards
Redux Toolkit store with 16 reducers across 24 service/slice/filter files
Vite build into Express dist/, Dockerfile, Docker Compose with MongoDB, public Render deploy

engineering_challenges.name: Cross-poll candidate exclusivity without transactions
engineering_challenges.why_hard: The invariant spans embedded arrays in sibling documents, so no unique index can enforce it; requires multi-document mutation with partial-success semantics and no transaction.

engineering_challenges.name: Optimistic-concurrency retry on embedded-array writes
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Mongoose VersionError on concurrent saves required detecting that specific error, re-reading state and bounding retries while letting other errors abort.
engineering_challenges.known_defect: const reassignment in the retry branch

engineering_challenges.name: Vote transfer with a denormalised counter
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Keeping voteCount consistent with the authoritative vote[] array across remove-then-add is a classic divergence trap.

engineering_challenges.name: Device-fingerprint step-up authentication from primitives
engineering_challenges.why_hard: User-agent parsing, a per-user allow-list, reversible encryption of a six-digit code, and an independently expiring token collection — built rather than imported.

engineering_challenges.name: Stripe webhook body-parser ordering
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Signature verification needs unparsed bytes; a global express.json() silently breaks it.

engineering_challenges.name: Same-origin SPA + API serving
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Required an asset-extension-aware fallback, anti-cache headers on index.html, and a build step copying dist/ into the server root — while local dev still runs cross-origin.

engineering_challenges.name: Two payment providers with incompatible state machines
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Stripe is session/webhook-driven; GoCardless is mandate/billing-request-driven with its own redirect flow — two state machines feeding one Payment collection.

decisions.problem: How to store candidates and votes
decisions.decision: Embed in Poll.options[] with a denormalised voteCount
decisions.reasoning: Reads are poll-shaped — one query renders a whole ballot
decisions.tradeoffs: Document growth; no unique index on voter; hand-enforced multi-document invariants; VersionError exposure
decisions.result: Workable at community scale, fragile under concurrency

decisions.problem: Where to keep the session token
decisions.tradeoffs: Requires CORS credentials config and HTTPS; no refresh rotation or server-side revocation

decisions.decision: Server-side middleware as authority, client-side components as UX mirror
decisions.reasoning: Server must be authoritative; client prevents dead-end UI
decisions.tradeoffs: Two places to change a rule
decisions.result: Correct pattern; one known mismatch at castVote
Half-migrated — deletePoll hard-deletes with the soft path commented out

decisions.decision: Replace Gmail OAuth2/Nodemailer with the Brevo API behind the same function signature
decisions.reasoning: API delivery avoids host SMTP restrictions
decisions.tradeoffs: Vendor lock-in; dead legacy code retained

decisions.decision: Monolith serving API and SPA from one Node process, containerised
decisions.tradeoffs: No independent scaling of static assets; build-time coupling

decisions.problem: Collecting both one-off and recurring money
decisions.decision: Stripe for cards, GoCardless for UK Direct Debit
decisions.reasoning: Different payment instruments for tickets vs dues
decisions.result: Incomplete — GoCardless abandoned at spike stage

lessons: Provider-shaped abstractions pay for themselves: the email swap touched one file because the signature was defined by the application, not the SDK — while the payment layer leaked Stripe concepts into the domain model and made the second provider a parallel path instead of a second implementation.
Embedded arrays trade query simplicity for invariant pain; a Vote collection with a compound unique index on (pollId, voterId) would have made the central rule a database guarantee.
Deployment surfaces a different class of bug than development — email, post-auth routing and SPA/API origin all broke only once deployed.
Enforce rules on the server and mirror them on the client; the one place the two disagree is exactly where a bug lives.
Every defect found in this audit is one an integration test would have caught; skipping tests was the costliest shortcut.
Choosing not to ship into an unstable adopter environment was judgement, not failure, and is defensible as such.

high_confidence_quantified: Designed and built a full-stack community-management platform (React 18 · Redux Toolkit · Node/Express · MongoDB) as sole developer across 85 commits and 10 months, comprising ~15,000 lines of application code, 59 REST endpoints, 8 data models and 16 Redux reducers.

Implemented a six-path authentication system — credentials, email verification, password reset, one-time login code, Google OAuth and Twitter/X OAuth — with bcrypt hashing, SHA-256 token hashing, encrypted time-limited login codes and HTTP-only JWT cookies.

Built an online election module supporting multiple concurrent polls, cross-poll candidate exclusivity, vote transfer with count reconciliation and verified-voter gating, enforced through a four-tier RBAC model across 59 endpoints.

Integrated Stripe (hosted Checkout, subscriptions with trial periods, Billing Portal, signature-verified webhooks) and GoCardless Direct Debit behind a single payment model, with server-side product resolution preventing client-supplied pricing.
Containerised and deployed the platform using Docker (node:20-alpine) and Docker Compose, serving a Vite-built SPA and the REST API from one same-origin Node process.
high_confidence_unquantified: Architected a MERN application end to end: schema design, REST API, authentication and authorisation, third-party integrations, state management, containerisation and deployment.
Migrated the transactional email layer between providers (Gmail OAuth2/Nodemailer → Brevo API) in response to a deployment-environment delivery failure, with zero changes to calling code.
Implemented optimistic-concurrency handling for concurrent writes to embedded document arrays, with bounded retry against re-read state.
Designed audit trails into the data model, capturing creator and an append-only edit history on every mutable entity.
requires_confirmation_or_work_first: Any claim about users, traffic, votes cast, payments processed, reliability or performance — none exist.
Test coverage, CI, monitoring — do not claim until added; adding them turns three documented weaknesses into honest new bullets.

interview_stories.title: Domain invariants under concurrency
interview_stories.situation: Candidates had to belong to exactly one poll per election, stored in embedded arrays across sibling documents
interview_stories.task: Enforce exclusivity without a unique index or transactions
interview_stories.action: Scan sibling polls, splice out, save, then push to target; batch-safe; distinguish 'moved' from 'added'; catch VersionError and retry against re-read state
interview_stories.result: Working exclusivity rule with clear organiser feedback
interview_stories.self_critique: A Vote collection with a compound unique index was the better design, and the retry has a const-reassignment bug

interview_stories.title: The bug that only existed after deploy
interview_stories.situation: Gmail OAuth2 email worked locally and silently stopped on the deployed host
interview_stories.action: Re-implemented against Brevo's API behind an identical function signature, pre-rendering Handlebars manually with ESM-safe path resolution
interview_stories.result: Email delivered via API, bypassing host SMTP restrictions; no call site changed

interview_stories.title: An auth stack built from primitives
interview_stories.action: bcrypt pre-save hook → SHA-256-hashed verification tokens → Cryptr-encrypted login codes with independent expiry → device allow-list triggering step-up auth → HTTP-only secure sameSite:none JWT cookie → server-side RBAC with a suspension check inside the guard
interview_stories.self_critique: Missing rate limiting, token rotation and revocation

interview_stories.title: Two payment providers, two state machines
interview_stories.action: Raw-body webhook ordering for signature verification; server-side fulfilment independent of the browser redirect; product names resolved from Stripe rather than trusted from the client
interview_stories.self_critique: GoCardless never progressed past a hard-coded spike

interview_stories.title: Deciding not to ship
interview_stories.situation: The intended adopter community entered a leadership dispute as the build became demonstrable
interview_stories.action: Stopped, de-branded the application and repositioned it as a portfolio artefact
interview_stories.result: Sunk cost separated from forward value

interview_stories.title: Seven hours stuck on role switching
interview_stories.evidence: commit 'After 7hours I couldn't figure out my desired switch role function', 2024-03-24, followed by sidebar state-management commits
interview_stories.action: Lifted role state into Redux instead of deriving it locally
